condition_other: circadian rhythm disruption (chronic jet lag model)
readout_other: TSE PhenoMaster locomotor activity; open field; plasma melatonin and cortisol ELISA; c-Fos immunofluorescence; HE, TUNEL, Nissl
direction_notes: LIFU to the SCN increased c-Fos in SCN, SPZ and DMH and reduced circadian phase difference, anxiety-like behaviour, melatonin and cortisol in jet-lagged mice.
safety_notes: HE, TUNEL and Nissl staining showed no tissue damage after stimulation.

timing.protocol_description: Total stimulation 10 minutes, pulse trains every 5 s; each train 200 ms with 2 ms tone bursts at PRF 250 Hz (4 ms period); daily in the morning for three consecutive days.

source_quotes.n_subjects: They were randomly divided into wild type (WT; normal mice without any treatment), chronic jet lag (CJL; model group), and US-stimulated SCN (US-SCN; LIFU-treated CJL mice) (n=8 per group).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Starting on Day 0, the US-SCN group received LIFU stimulation targeting the SCN in the morning for three consecutive days.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In this study, the US was delivered using a 1 MHz miniaturized focused transducer made of PZT-4, with a diameter of approximately 19mm.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: Each pulse train comprised a sonication duration of 200 ms, with individual pulses exhibiting a toneburst duration (TBD) of 2 ms and a pulse repetition frequency of 250 Hz, corresponding to a pulse repetition period (PRP) of 4 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Each pulse train comprised a sonication duration of 200 ms, with individual pulses exhibiting a toneburst duration (TBD) of 2 ms and a pulse repetition frequency of 250 Hz, corresponding to a pulse repetition period (PRP) of 4 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Each pulse train comprised a sonication duration of 200 ms, with individual pulses exhibiting a toneburst duration (TBD) of 2 ms and a pulse repetition frequency of 250 Hz, corresponding to a pulse repetition period (PRP) of 4 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: The transducer was positioned transcranially, generating a peak acoustic pressure of 0.43 MPa at the skull surface.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: The transducer was positioned transcranially, generating a peak acoustic pressure of 0.43 MPa at the skull surface. After accounting for an estimated 18% transcranial attenuation, the efective intracranial pressure at the target site was approximately 0.35 MPa.

flags.reason: n=8 per group for three groups; only the US-SCN group (8) was sonicated, the safety-assessment cohort size is not stated.
0.43 MPa described as peak acoustic pressure at the skull surface; domain not otherwise stated.
0.35 MPa obtained by the authors from an estimated 18% transcranial attenuation (derating), not measured.
No transducer maker named; only PZT-4 material, 19 mm diameter.
Whether mice were awake or anaesthetised during sonication is not stated.
